title: Milestones and the tree through one door
done_when: `foreman milestone add|split|merge` keeps history and a change count; `foreman node add` is the one write door with the six refusals of decision 6, append-only and folded on read; `foreman front import` reads fronts/<name>/{map.md,milestones.jsonl,tree.jsonl} into the runtime; this front's own files are imported on the live installation. title: Reservations and the mechanical job queue
done_when: A front reserves its team exclusively while it runs; `foreman job queue|cancel|front|edit` are the supervisor's only job verbs; the collector starts a queued job when its model has a free reserved slot, its dependencies finished and the team policy allows; the queue states why each item waits; the worker's page is rendered from the node, the map facts it names and the role sheet, and a job with no sheet is refused. Shared mutable resources are reserved with a count; reservations are phased (builders first, reviewers when a head exists); Muse runs only mechanical leaves in idempotent units; a node may depend on another front's output; a reviewer that died on quota or an access flag is its own recorded state and both attempts of a retried review are kept; review rounds have a budget and after two rounds finding the same class the node returns to the supervisor; role boundaries are enforced by tool permission.

title: Landing as a queued script with per-repository policy
done_when: A landing item at two levels (job branch onto the front branch, front branch onto its target) is started by the runtime under a lock, updates onto the target's remote head, runs the repository's check in a fresh worktree, pushes or opens the PR per the repository's policy, records command, exit, duration, output file and head, and on failure files a finding with the output to the requesting supervisor; a job with no recorded verify is refused; the rebase of an open front when its target moved runs per repository. Evidence is bound to head plus base and a target move marks it stale; the rebase item precedes the landing item; the script refuses an empty range, runs the check after the update on the tree that lands, records commits dropped by rebase, and a policy may name a landing script; a flake register and green as a count for checks run under contention.
